Chase88,
 
Sell your laptop and boycott Dell consumer products moving forward.. This is a wide spread issue that began with a BIOS update and Dell refuses to fix it. There is no known *Reliable* solution. Some folks have success with solutions found on various forms. Others found success with half-assed suggestions from Dell about updating to the latest drivers and using dell power manager to set thermal profile to ultra performance.
What we need is a BIOS version that does not have this issue..
Personally, I have not had success with any solutions and I'm a seasoned IT veteran. Everyone who is frustrated by this issue has a valid reason to be and it is down right ridiculous that an issue like this even exists.
 
This laptop was good back before the BIOS update, now it is a glorified desktop that requires an AC adapter to be usable.,Negative

You will need to get the two bios of both chips in the motherboard, and the principal one needs to be clear on the ME region in the BIOS. 
This ME region tells the motherboard the especifications of the machine, and when it is already write, the machine will not acept it because it is different from the true especifications and informations of your own notebook. 
It is a very difficult process, but you can get onde of those bios with clear ME in some forums,Positive
